metaDescription: Nutter Fort, Harrison County mineral owners: Clarksburg-adjacent legacy production, subdivided residential lots, and severed mineral title work.
heroLead: Nutter Fort sits just outside Clarksburg in Harrison County, where residential development has grown over mineral estates severed decades earlier.
intro: As a small Harrison County community adjacent to Clarksburg, Nutter Fort has seen its surface acreage largely built out into residential and small commercial use, while the mineral estate beneath much of that land was severed and traded separately long before the current houses were built.

sections.heading: Severed minerals under built-out ground
paragraphs: Because Nutter Fort's surface is largely residential, the current homeowner and the mineral owner are frequently unrelated parties, with the mineral interest tracked at the courthouse under a legal description that predates the subdivision plat. Confirming exactly which modern parcel corresponds to an older mineral severance takes a title review, not a glance at a current tax map.

sections.heading: Harrison County's legacy production history
paragraphs: Clarksburg-area acreage, including tracts around Nutter Fort, has a production history reaching back well before the Marcellus era, with older leases and wellbores still on record for some tracts. Whether your interest is under an active lease, an older flat-rate arrangement, or nothing currently producing depends on the individual parcel's history.

sections.heading: Matching an old legal description to a current Nutter Fort parcel
paragraphs: Because Nutter Fort's residential development postdates many of the underlying mineral severances, the legal description on an older deed sometimes doesn't match the boundaries shown on a current property survey or tax map. Reconciling the two takes a title professional working from the original metes-and-bounds description forward.
This step matters before any sale, since a buyer needs a clear match between the recorded mineral tract and its actual location relative to current development and any nearby wellbores.

faqs.question: Do I own minerals under my Nutter Fort house if I own the house?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily — many mineral estates in this area were severed from the surface before current residential development, so the mineral owner and surface owner are often separate.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my family holds a severed mineral interest near Nutter Fort?
faqs.answer: A courthouse records check tracing your family name against the Harrison County deed books, independent of current tax records, will confirm whether an interest exists.

faqs.question: Is there active drilling near Nutter Fort?
faqs.answer: Legacy production exists in the area; current activity on any specific tract depends on lease status, which is worth confirming individually.

faqs.question: What if my deed's legal description doesn't match my current tax map at all?
faqs.answer: That's common with older severances predating current development; a title professional can reconcile the two using the original survey description.
